result:
Round 388 passed and is published, so the next round is a regression round: **round 389 = REGRESSION-2026-11-08, part 1**. A changes no code this round; C runs the browser checks. Decision: **CONTINUE**. Nothing outside the loop is blocking.

**Round 388 result** (I checked C's evidence files myself):
- After a playback failure the meters now drop to −∞ at both screen sizes (1440×900 and 1280×720), and the clock stops.
- The covering tests pass: 66 files, 1,026 tests. All 16 deliberately broken versions of the code were caught.
- The gate published it as commit `11ca746`, which is the baseline for the next round. The store tree is clean.
- Six bugs are now closed: C-R387-01, GATE-B385-M2, A-R386-REVIEW-M1, B-R386-UNGUARDED-GRAPH-CALLERS, TL-R387-M1 and A-R386-REVIEW-L1.

**Why the regression starts now:** the three-day rule only makes it mandatory from 2026-11-08, so this is one day early. The previous planning (D-29z1309) had already set it for this round. Rounds 385–388 also changed shared playback code, and the workflow lists that as a reason to re-check finished features. `regression-last.json` is left alone until the whole regression closes.

**What round 389 checks:**
- The regression entry in the backlog had no scope list, so I wrote one. Every item finished in rounds 343–388 is a named browser check at both screen sizes, ordered newest risk first:
  - playback-failure stop and meter drop;
  - Play refused while audio is still decoding;
  - streaming WAV export;
  - the components that now re-render separately (perf work);
  - the status line;
  - stem cache;
  - video drag;
  - faders and icons;
  - group move;
  - a product-page-to-export walk-through.
- One new check comes from the code reviewer's first Low (L1). It has the pump fall behind while a failure is forced, and expects the same stopped state with meters at −∞. The browser can't tell which code path failed, so that part stays a unit-test candidate.
- After the browser checks:
  - the perf suite runs alone. Its config serves all 4 specs from one production server.
  - the perf library tests, the smoke tests and the anonymous auth check follow.
- Round 390 is part 2 (everything up to round 342, using the round-340 template), then PERF-13b-ii. A Medium or worse finding becomes the next round's fix first.
- `b-round-388/claims-389.sh` re-checks every fact the task states about current code. It also confirms that every script the task cites exists. The tracked files are frozen in a 1,284-file checksum list.

**Backlog (v356, decisions D-29z1310…1315):**
- The reviewer's four Lows are deferred to the polish list.
- The reviewer's architecture note is recorded as a signal, plus an unscheduled test-only candidate (a shared fake Web Audio helper). This is the fourth round in a row on the same playback code.
- I added a note to the existing root architecture-checkpoint request instead of opening a new one. It doesn't block anything, but the answer is wanted before PERF-13b-ii.
- `feature-status.md` and `b-next.json` are updated (62 remaining ids).
- `tasks/round-388.md` is a byte-identical copy of the old task.

**Advisor:** available and used twice, before writing and at the close. At the close it caught two problems I fixed:
- I had placed the new test-helper candidate ahead of PERF-13b-ii in the queue. It now sits with the other test-only items.
- I had invented a pixel threshold for the icon check. It now uses round 346's own comparison.

C's round-388 working copy (`c-round-388/tree/`) is still in the loop folder. I left it for the next retro to note, since it isn't mine to delete.
